results.proof: In the original image L,P,M are collinear in that order; K,P,T are collinear in that order; K,Q,M are collinear in that order. P,Q,K,L lie on C₁ and P,Q,M on C₂, with PT tangent to C₂ at P. Thus ∠LPK=∠MPT by vertically opposite angles. The tangent–chord theorem for chord PM gives ∠MPT=∠MQP. Since QM extends QK, ∠MQP is the exterior angle at Q of cyclic quadrilateral P Q K L, and equals the opposite interior angle ∠PLK. Thus ∠LPK=∠PLK, so opposite sides KL=PK. The raw solution incorrectly identifies ∠MQP with ∠LKP; the candidate corrects the proof and explicitly preserves the raw error. The native coordinates place P,Q,K,L on C₁, P,Q,M on C₂ and preserve the stated collinearities and tangent; the P–Q chord is present. Coordinates are unlabelled construction, with no marked additional given. Pages 25 and 28 teach the cyclic exterior-angle and alternate-segment properties; combining them across circles is ordinary transfer. This two-circle isosceles proof is distinct from the current tangent–secant equation and other owners.
